heading: INT. FROZEN FOOD WAREHOUSE, WALK-IN FREEZER - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FROZEN FOOD WAREHOUSE, WALK-IN FREEZER - NIGHT
Steel racks of frosted boxes.
A vapor cloud rolls off every breath.
The door is frozen shut.
ROSALIND "ROZ" PETKOVIC (30s, thermal jacket, night inventory clipboard) crouches beside the door, pounding the latch.
Behind her, her coworker DENNIS ABERNATHY-VOSS (40s, beard stiff with frost) paces the aisle.
Between them, hunched on a pallet of peas, sits a stranger in a soaked tuxedo: LAZARUS BELL (50s, slow-blinking, shivering).
It's jammed!
units.name: ROZ

units.text: Hit it harder!
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: I am hitting it!
units.name: ROZ

units.text: Dennis shoves her aside and throws his shoulder into the door.
It doesn't budge.
They both slump against it, panting.
Lazarus lifts his head.
It will not open.
units.name: LAZARUS

units.text: Who the hell are you?
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: A man in the wrong place.
units.name: LAZARUS

units.text: How did you get in here?
units.name: ROZ

units.text: I walked in. Hours ago. Perhaps days.
units.name: LAZARUS

units.text: Days? We've been here forty minutes.
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: You have been here forty minutes. I have been here longer.
units.name: LAZARUS

units.text: He stands.
His breath doesn't fog.
Roz sees it first and backs away, clipboard hugged to her chest.
Dennis.
units.name: ROZ

units.text: What?
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: Look at his breath.
units.name: ROZ

units.text: Dennis looks.
Lazarus smiles, apologetic, and spreads his hands.
I have found it is easier not to tell people.
units.name: LAZARUS

units.text: Tell people what?
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: Only that it does not get warmer. That is all.
units.name: LAZARUS

units.text: Roz grabs Dennis by the sleeve and they both charge the door again, slamming into it together, again and again, until it cracks and bursts open on a blast of loading-dock air.
They tumble out onto asphalt.
Roz scrambles to look back.
The freezer door swings gently shut.
Through the shrinking gap, Lazarus raises a hand in farewell.
